coordinates.locator: geometry:modane-lsm-underground (OpenStreetMap-georeferenced underground laboratory point, accuracy 100 m)
coordinates.note: Point for the laboratory inside the Fréjus tunnel, georeferenced from OpenStreetMap; it is shown as approximate because an OpenStreetMap tracing is not a survey. It replaces the Carré Sciences surface outreach building in Modane, 6.4 km from the laboratory.

depth_mwe.note: Average overburden of the laboratory under the Fréjus mountain; Pandola 2011 gives 4000 m w.e. as the minimum and 4800 m w.e. as the average. EDELWEISS also gives a rock overburden of 1800 m at zero degrees, against the 1700 m on the site record. Mei & Hime 2006 Table I derive an equivalent flat-overburden depth of 4.15 ± 0.2 km.w.e. from the Fréjus flux.
depth_mwe.quote: an average rock overburden of 4800 m w. e. (meters water equivalent)

muon_flux.note: Muons per square metre per day. The paper states that Sec. 3.6 determines "the integral muon flux through a horizontal surface", from the EDELWEISS muon-veto system (18503 candidates in 2009-2010, muon bundles included, no zenith-angle cut); the same data give 6.6 per m^2 per day through a sphere. The quote is the PDF text with the superscript 2 of m^2 lost in extraction. Pandola 2011 quotes 5.76 × 10^-5 m^-2 s^-1, "five muons per m2 per day", from the Fréjus experiment (Berger et al. 1989); Mei & Hime Table I: (5.47 ± 0.1) × 10^-9 cm^-2 s^-1 (Fréjus).
muon_flux.quote: Souterrain de Modane (LSM) was measured to be Φµ = (5.4 ± 0.2+0.5 −0.9 ) muons/m /d

summary.plain: A laboratory carved into the rock in the middle of a road tunnel through the Alps, under 1700 metres of mountain, near Modane, France.
summary.technical: Underground experimental hall mid-way through the Frejus road tunnel (Modane, Savoie), under ~1700 m of rock; address Carre Sciences, 1125 route de Bardonneche, 73500 Modane.
